adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses `&&` instead of `||` in `addGuests.handler.ts:44-46`, requiring the user to be both an admin and an owner instead of either

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to satisfy both checks. Given the variable name and the subsequent authorization gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`), this will deny access to a team admin who is not also the team owner (or vice versa), which is a concrete, verifiable authorization/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw `guests` array passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests` in `addGuests.handler.ts:146`, causing existing attendees to receive the wrong email template

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). Only `uniqueGuests` are actually inserted into the booking via `createMany`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the template selection is driven by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`: those included get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, others get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the input `guests` contains an email of an existing attendee (which is possible; it’s filtered out from DB but not rejected as long as there’s at least one truly new guest), that existing attendee will incorrectly be treated as a “new guest” and receive the scheduled/invite email instead of the “guests added” notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-sending failures are silently swallowed in `addGuests.handler.ts:150-153`, showing a success toast to the user even though notification emails may have failed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` afterward. On the client, `AddGuestsDialog` shows a success toast in `onSuccess` of the mutation. Therefore, even if `sendAddGuestsEmails` fails, the mutation still succeeds and the UI reports success without any indication that notification emails were not sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` in `addGuests.handler.ts:42-43` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to be both team admin and owner simultaneously, which blocks non-owner admins from adding guests

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to satisfy both predicates simultaneously. In the subsequent permission check:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN
```

a user who is a team admin but not a team owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be denied (unless they are also the organizer/attendee). That matches the finding: the `&&` makes the permission stricter than “admin OR owner” and likely blocks non-owner admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` environment variable is introduced without documentation, `.env.example` update, or validation in `addGuests.handler.ts:74-76`

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new optional environment variable read (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`) in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but the code safely handles it being absent by defaulting to an empty array, so there is no correctness/bug defect introduced. The claims about missing documentation or `.env.example` updates are not verifiable from the diff alone (those files/changes are simply not part of this patch), and lack of “validation” is not a clear defect here since the input is already email-validated by the zod schema and the env var is only used as a best-effort blacklist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling around `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` in `addGuests.handler.ts:135`, which can leave the booking's attendee list out of sync with the calendar if the call throws

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error out after the DB has already been updated, leaving the booking attendee list updated in the database while the external calendar update did not occur (i.e., out of sync). The diff shows error handling only for `sendAddGuestsEmails`, not for the calendar update call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts:536-540` silently swallows errors with only a `console.log`, leaving users unaware that notification emails failed to send

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, and that function does not catch or swallow errors—it `await`s `Promise.all(emailsToSend)` and will reject on failure. The only silent swallowing is in `addGuests.handler.ts`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and still returns success. So the finding as stated (blaming `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts:536-540`) is a misattribution/misread of the diff.

The diff provides no evidence of an actual mismatch or resulting bug—only that a type assertion is used. Also, validation does not “always fail on first interaction”: if the user types a valid email into the initially-rendered field, the value becomes a valid email string and parsing succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic bug using `&&` instead of `||` in `addGuests.handler.ts:38-39`, requiring both admin AND owner instead of either

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check, which contradicts the name and typical intent (“admin OR owner”). As written, a user who is only an admin (or only an owner) will not be treated as authorized via this path, making the authorization logic overly restrictive and likely incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization query bypasses tenancy on booking in `addGuests.handler.ts:22-35` by filtering `prisma.booking.findFirst` only by `id` with no scoping

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is indeed fetched with `where: { id: bookingId }` only, but the mutation does not rely on that query as an authorization gate. Immediately after fetching, it enforces explicit authorization (`isTeamAdmin/Owner` for the booking’s `eventType.teamId`, or organizer, or existing attendee) and throws `FORBIDDEN` otherwise. That means the lack of scoping in the Prisma query does not, by itself, allow cross-tenant access to add guests (i.e., no verifiable “tenancy bypass” is demonstrated by the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race condition on duplicate-email check in `addGuests.handler.ts:75-80` vs `:84` due to lack of transaction or unique index

adjudication.rationale: `addGuestsHandler` reads the current attendees (`booking.attendees`) and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already present, then later does a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. Because this is not done in a transaction and the duplicate check is based on a potentially stale snapshot, two concurrent calls can both pass the `!booking.attendees.some(...)` check for the same email and then both attempt to insert it. The diff also doesn’t add any DB-level uniqueness constraint or `skipDuplicates`/upsert logic here, so the “check then insert” pattern is a classic TOCTOU window that can lead to duplicate attendee rows or a unique-constraint error under concurrency (if such a constraint exists elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `updateCalendarAttendees` and email send are outside the DB transaction in `addGuests.handler.ts:84-137`, risking DB/calendar drift

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the Prisma update that persists new attendees (`prisma.booking.update` with `createMany`) happens before calling external side-effects: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no surrounding `prisma.$transaction` or compensating rollback logic. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not wrapped in try/catch), the handler will error after the DB has already been modified, leaving the DB state updated while the external calendar was not—i.e., a real drift/inconsistency risk introduced by the ordering and lack of transaction/compensation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failure silently swallowed in `addGuests.handler.ts:136-139`, logging without the `err` object and returning success
Non-idempotent handler with no idempotency key in `addGuests.handler.ts`, allowing duplicate rows/updates/emails on retry

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` is not explicitly idempotent via an idempotency key, but the diff does not show it “allowing duplicate rows/updates/emails on retry” in a verifiable way. On each invocation it re-reads the booking (including `attendees`) and computes `uniqueGuests` by excluding emails already present in `booking.attendees`; a retry with the same payload after a successful first run will result in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` before performing `createMany` or sending emails. Duplicate inserts would only be possible under concurrent/racing requests and/or lack of a DB uniqueness constraint, neither of which is established by the diff, so the finding as stated is not strictly supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(n·m) linear scan and case-sensitivity mismatch in `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `email-manager.ts:538` due to inconsistent email normalization
Blacklist via env var with linear scan and magic-string config in `addGuests.handler.ts:70-74`, which doesn't trim whitespace and is hard to evolve

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the blacklist is built from `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` with no `.trim()`. If the env var contains comma-separated values with spaces (e.g. `"bad@example.com, other@example.com"`), the second entry becomes `" other@example.com"` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` will not match a normal `guest` value, so blacklisting can silently fail. The rest of the finding ("linear scan" / "hard to evolve") is more subjective, but the whitespace issue is a concrete correctness problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `booking.userId || 0` fallback in `addGuests.handler.ts:48-53` hides missing organizer and passes `0` to functions, causing opaque errors

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup is `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (which is plausible since the code also uses `booking.userId || 0` and earlier `booking.userId === user.id`), this will query for user id `0` and then throw a Prisma “record not found” error. That behavior both (a) obscures the real issue (missing/invalid organizer on the booking) and (b) relies on a magic fallback id rather than a clear TRPCError. This is directly verifiable from the diff; the fallback can cause opaque runtime errors when `userId` is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Schema accepts empty `guests` array in `addGuests.schema.ts:4-6` but handler rejects it late in `addGuests.handler.ts:82`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` allows an empty array because no `.min(1)` is specified. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the request is only rejected later: `uniqueGuests` can be `[]` (e.g., when `guests` is empty), and then it throws `TRPCError` when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`. This means invalid input passes schema validation and is handled as a runtime/business-rule error instead of being caught at the input-validation layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` is not enforced on the server schema in `addGuests.schema.ts`, allowing duplicates
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: duplicates can be submitted (e.g., repeated emails) and, without server-side enforcement/deduplication, duplicate attendee rows can be inserted. The candidate frames it as client-side uniqueness not being enforced on the server, which aligns with the golden issue about missing deduplication before createMany.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail` initial state `['']` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:31` breaks the empty rendering path in `MultiEmail.tsx`

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog the state is initialized to `[""]`, so `MultiEmail` sees `value.length === 1` and renders an empty `EmailField` rather than the "no emails yet" button path (`!value.length`). That does not break `MultiEmail`—it’s simply choosing the non-empty rendering branch. The component still works (shows an input), and nothing in the diff indicates that the empty-branch UI is required for correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail` uses array index as React key in `MultiEmail.tsx:38`, causing incorrect state retention on removal/reorder

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list rendering uses `key={index}` for each `EmailField` (`value.map((field, index) => ( <li key={index}> ... ))`). Because the component supports removing an entry via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`, remaining items shift indices after removal. With index keys, React reuses component instances for different emails after a deletion, which can lead to stale/internal state (e.g., focus, validation state inside `EmailField`, or other per-item state) being retained and associated with the wrong row. This is a known correctness/UX issue in dynamic lists where items can be removed/reordered, and the diff introduces exactly that pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `replyTo` in `organizer-add-guests-email.ts:29` leaks all attendee emails to every recipient, creating a privacy/PII leak

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the nodemailer payload sets `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This embeds every attendee email address into the email headers for each recipient of the organizer/team email (`to` is the organizer or a team member). Email headers (including Reply-To) are visible to recipients, so each recipient can see the full attendee email list, which is a concrete privacy/PII leak introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` component passes `subject` as a translation key string in `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx:6` but the class-based template ignores it, causing drift

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the class-based template `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` explicitly sets the email subject using `this.t("guests_added_event_type_subject", ...)`. The React component `packages/emails/src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx` also passes `subject="guests_added_event_type_subject"` to `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. Even if the NodeMailer class does not read the React component’s `subject` prop (not shown here), there is no verifiable drift introduced by this diff because both sides use the same translation key for the subject. The finding claims a mismatch/ignored prop causing drift, but that is not demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `attendeesListPromises` reloads ALL attendees (N translation fetches) on every guest add in `addGuests.handler.ts:94-107`, an unbounded N+1 I/O pattern

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, after updating the booking, the code builds `attendeesListPromises` by mapping over `bookingAttendees.attendees` (which is the full attendee list, not just newly added guests) and for each attendee it does `translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")`. That is one `getTranslation(...)` call per attendee on every add-guests mutation, so the work scales linearly with total attendees and repeats for attendees/locales that may already have been loaded. This matches the reported unbounded per-attendee I/O/N+1 style pattern (even though it’s run via Promise.all, it’s still N separate loads).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `evt` built from pre-update `booking` while `attendees` comes from post-update in `addGuests.handler.ts:110-130`, a maintainability hazard for future fields

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler first fetches `booking`, then performs `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... } }, include: { attendees: true } })` and uses `bookingAttendees.attendees` to build `attendeesList`. The `evt` object is then built mostly from the original `booking` (title, description, start/end, uid, location, eventType, destinationCalendar, references) and only `attendees` is sourced from the updated attendees list. Since the only mutation performed here is adding attendees, those other `booking` fields are not changed by this update, so there is no verifiable correctness bug introduced in the diff. The proposed finding is a speculative/maintainability concern rather than a real defect observable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE` in `_router.tsx:18,79` has no invalidation and uses cargo-culted dead defense `if (!cache) throw`

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` to the existing `UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE` lazy-import pattern in `_router.tsx`: it conditionally imports the handler once and stores it. Having “no invalidation” is expected for a module-level cache of imported handlers and is not a correctness/security bug introduced by this change. The follow-up `if (!UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE.addGuests) throw` is explicitly commented as unreachable and only exists to satisfy type safety; it does not create a functional defect. This finding is therefore a style/design critique rather than a verifiable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to new guests in `email-manager.ts:540-544` instead of a purpose-built template, causing semantic mismatch
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over the full `calendarEvent.attendees` but decides which template to send based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` where `newGuests` is the input guests list, leading to incorrect template selection for recipients. The candidate flags that the function sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to new guests instead of the intended add-guests template, which is essentially the same underlying problem (wrong template selection for new guests), even if it doesn’t explicitly mention the full-attendees-vs-newGuests array mismatch mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both admin and owner to add guests, incorrectly forbidding team admins who are not owners

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Despite the name implying an OR condition, this requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
will therefore incorrectly forbid team admins who are not owners (and vice versa if those roles are distinct).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog initial state is `useState<string[]>([""])` which makes the `handleAdd` length guard never trigger, causing empty string to fail Zod email validation with no user action; empty strings should be filtered out before validation

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, multiEmailValue is initialized to [""] and reset to [""] on success/cancel. handleAdd only early-returns when multiEmailValue.length === 0, which will never be true with this initialization. If the user clicks “Add” without entering any email, ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse([""]) fails because "" is not a valid email, and the dialog shows the invalid-email error instead of treating it as “no input”/no-op. Filtering out empty strings (or initializing with []) would make the length guard meaningful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on Cancel button click, not on dialog open or when `multiEmailValue` changes, causing error message to persist if dialog is closed via `onOpenChange` and reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. The dialog can be closed via `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>` (e.g., clicking outside/ESC), which does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Reopening the dialog will therefore keep showing the error message. Also, changing `multiEmailValue` after an invalid attempt does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so the error can persist even after correcting inputs unless Cancel is clicked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block declares `err` but logs only a static string instead of the actual error, making email failure debugging impossible

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` catch block captures `err` but never logs it or otherwise surfaces details. This is directly verifiable in the diff and reduces debuggability/observability of email-send failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends an `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to the organizer and then also sends one to each `teamMember`, causing duplicate emails when the organizer is also in `team.members`

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code unconditionally queues one `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` with no `teamMember` (which will send to `calendarEvent.organizer.email`), and then, if `calendarEvent.team?.members` exists, it loops over every `teamMember` and queues another `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` for each. The `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` implementation uses `this.teamMember?.email || this.calEvent.organizer.email` as the recipient, so if the organizer is also present in `calendarEvent.team.members`, their email address will be included in the loop and they will receive a second identical organizer email. There is no deduplication logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Menu item `id` and dialog `data-testid="add_members"` use "members" terminology while everything else uses "guests", causing inconsistency and brittle test selectors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce inconsistent terminology: the new menu item uses `id: "add_members"` and the Add button uses `data-testid="add_members"`, while UI strings and feature naming consistently use “guests” (`additional_guests`, `guests_added`, etc.). However, this is a naming/consistency nit rather than a functional/correctness defect; nothing in the shown diff relies on the `id` value or the `data-testid` for runtime behavior, and the claim about “brittle test selectors” is speculative without tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail.tsx` reassigns the `value` prop directly with `value = value || []`, which is an anti-pattern; should use a local variable instead

adjudication.rationale: In `MultiEmail.tsx`, the line `value = value || []` does reassign the function parameter, but in React this does not mutate the parent prop object—it only rebinds the local parameter variable. In the diff, `value` is typed as `string[]` (not optional), and the reassignment is simply a defensive fallback. This is at most a style/lint preference ("no param reassign" / "don’t reassign props") rather than a verifiable bug or correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email blacklist bypass: blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not lowercased before `.includes()` check, allowing attackers to bypass the blacklist by varying email casing.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but the incoming guest email is not, so the `.includes()` check can be bypassed using uppercase/mixed-case emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Information disclosure and spam amplification: any booking attendee can add an unbounded number of arbitrary guests, leaking video meeting credentials (URL and password) to arbitrary email addresses without rate limiting or limits.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and it permits the action if `isAttendee` is true (no requirement to be organizer/admin). The input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and the handler has no rate limiting or caps, so an attendee can submit an arbitrarily large list. The handler then (1) persists the new attendees via `createMany` and (2) builds a `CalendarEvent` including `videoCallData` (meeting URL/password) when a `_video` reference exists, and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which will email attendees about the event. This enables an attendee to cause invitations/emails containing meeting details to be sent to arbitrary external addresses (spam amplification + disclosure of meeting join info).
